item.title: China leads development of 78 international standards on AI
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
China leads development of 78 international standards on AI BEIJING, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- China has spearheaded the development of 78 international standards on artificial intelligence (AI), turning its industrial practices and technological innovations into global public goods, according to the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). Sun Wei, deputy head of the department of standards innovation under the SAMR, told a press conference Tuesday that the body has made active efforts to help improve the international standards system architecture for AI. Working with leading companies and top research institutions, the SAMR has led the development of 29 foundational and common international standards, covering key areas that include data governance, human-computer interaction, security and trustworthiness, Sun said. In addition, the SAMR has coordinated the efforts of 15 technical standards bodies in developing 49 international standards for sector-specific applications, including smart cities and intelligent manufacturing, according to the official. Sectoral application standards act as a key lever to drive the scaled and standardized implementation of AI technologies. In recent years, the SAMR has expanded its efforts to advance international standards in key areas, such as smart manufacturing, smart cities, smart logistics and smart water management, drawing on China's extensive application scenarios and mature industrial practices. Sun said China's systematic efforts to develop application-oriented standards across multiple industries offered technical standards and practical solutions for wider international adoption, supporting AI-empowered real economy development and inclusive, shared digital transformation. The SAMR also revealed that, in response to common risks such as deepfakes and model "poisoning" in generative AI, China has jointly developed with multiple countries a guideline on addressing risks in generative AI. According to the SAMR, this marked the world's first international standards proposal targeting generative AI governance and can provide key support for promoting the formation of a global consensus on risk management. item.title: Commentary: China's space station opens a new chapter in int'l cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
Commentary: China's space station opens a new chapter in int'l cooperation This undated photo shows Shenzhou-24 crew members Tang Hongbo (C), Wu Yi (R), and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali. (Xinhua) BEIJING, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- The Shenzhou-24 mission marks a milestone in China's manned space program as a Pakistani astronaut becomes the first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong space station, opening a new chapter in China's efforts to advance international cooperation in space exploration. Over the years, China has built its space station through independent innovation and technological development, demonstrating its growing capabilities in manned spaceflight. Its experience shows that self-reliance and international cooperation are not mutually exclusive. While independent development has laid a solid foundation for China's space program, openness is creating new opportunities for its continued progress. China has increasingly sought to make its space program more accessible to international partners, offering opportunities for other countries to participate in scientific research and space exploration. The Shenzhou-24 mission is a concrete step in this direction. For Pakistan, the mission offers an opportunity to develop expertise in human spaceflight, strengthen its astronaut training capabilities and participate in scientific experiments in orbit. For China, it marks the first joint spaceflight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts, extending bilateral cooperation into a new frontier. The experience could also pave the way for broader international participation in China's space program. Space exploration transcends national borders and offers opportunities for countries to advance scientific knowledge through cooperation. China has consistently advocated the peaceful use of outer space and promoted international collaboration in this field. A case in point is China's recent donation to the United Nations of a lunar soil sample collected by the Chang'e-6 mission from the far side of the Moon. By sharing the fruits of its space exploration with the international community, China is helping create opportunities for joint research and enabling more countries to benefit from advances in space science. This photo taken on Sept. 14, 2026 shows a lunar sample collected from the far side of the Moon by China's Chang'e-6 mission, in Vienna, Austria. (Xinhua/He Canling) Space exploration should not be an exclusive endeavor, but a shared undertaking that brings countries together through the exchange of knowledge, technology and talent. By opening its space station to international partners, China is creating opportunities for scientific collaboration and contributing to the peaceful use of outer space. item.title: Working together to turn the vision of building an Asia-Pacific community into reality
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
Working together to turn the vision of building an Asia-Pacific community into reality Photo shows the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC)-themed flower beds on a street in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong province. (Photo/Weng Qiyu) Along Shenzhen Bay in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong province, calm waters stretch along broad, open shores. On Nov. 19, the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting was held in the city, bringing together participants to discuss ways to advance Asia-Pacific cooperation and promote regional development. Chinese President Xi Jinping chaired the meeting and delivered a speech, proposing to work together to build the "four key pillars" of an Asia-Pacific community -- economy and trade, connectivity, innovation, and development. He charted the course toward an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development. Drawing on lessons from the past helps pave the way for a new journey ahead. Since its establishment more than three decades ago, APEC has kept pace with the times and steered the process of Asia-Pacific economic integration. Over the years, the Asia-Pacific region has witnessed progress with each passing day, and created the Asia-Pacific miracle of rapid economic growth. Today, changes unseen in a century are unfolding at an accelerating pace across the globe. Innovation is burgeoning across sciences, technologies, and industries. In the face of new opportunities and challenges, how can the region write a new chapter of the Asia-Pacific miracle? Taking into account the broader historical trends and the demands of the times, Xi pointed out that building an Asia-Pacific community requires commitment to solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, and inclusive development. These four principles outline the vision for an Asia-Pacific community from four dimensions: relations among economies, the path to development, the driving force for progress, and the values that underpin the community. They provide fundamental guidance for building an Asia-Pacific community and ensuring steady, sustained progress in regional cooperation. Turning this vision into reality calls for concrete action, resolve, and a strong sense of responsibility. "China is an advocate, promoter, and forerunner of Asia-Pacific economic cooperation. We would like to work with all parties to pool wisdom and synergy in building the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community," Xi said in his speech. He called on APEC economies to strengthen the pillar of economy and trade. "The Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific (FTAAP) is a shared vision of APEC members. It is important to make steady progress in realizing this vision and setting a higher standard for openness," he said. He called for APEC economies to upgrade the pillar of connectivity and strengthen physical connectivity by improving the infrastructure network, deepen institutional connectivity by harmonizing policies and regulations, and enhance people-to-people connectivity by facilitating travel for business, tourism and other purposes, further strengthening the ties that underpin regional economic integration. APEC economies should foster the pillar of innovation and make the digital economy and artificial intelligence (AI) the engines of innovation-driven growth, Xi said. He also urged APEC economies to enhance the pillar of development and strengthen capacity building, achieve sustainable economic growth, and tap into the full potential of talent across the Asia-Pacific. At the meeting, Xi also announced a series of new measures China will take to support Asia-Pacific cooperation. Addressing both immediate concerns and long-term trends, these proposals and measures demonstrate China's commitment to translating its vision for an Asia-Pacific community into concrete results and reflect its sense of responsibility as a major country. China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and has consistently supported regional cooperation. Since assuming the role of host of APEC 2026, China has held more than 300 meetings and events in 16 cities, attracting over 10,000 representatives from APEC member economies. Their active participation has helped ensure that the APEC "China Year" deliver meaningful outcomes. Various parties have spoken highly of the fruitful results achieved during the APEC "China Year," expressing their readiness to deepen cooperation across various fields, jointly address risks and challenges, and promote APEC's further development, thereby contributing to peace, stability, and prosperity in the region and the world. With firm confidence, a clear sense of direction, and a commitment to delivering results, economies across the region have come together to build an Asia-Pacific community. China stands ready to work with all parties to remain committed to this overarching goal and advance cooperation across all fields with a strong sense of mission. Together, they can deliver more tangible outcomes from Asia-Pacific cooperation and write a new chapter in the Asia-Pacific miracle. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Traditional rice wine brewing boosts local economy in Kengtou Village, China's Jiangxi
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
Traditional rice wine brewing boosts local economy in Kengtou Village, China's Jiangxi Winemaker Zhan Rongbin seals the rice wine in jars for fermentation in Kengtou Village of Wuyuan County, east China's Jiangxi Province, Nov. 24, 2026. Leveraging its history and culture of wine-making, Kengtou Village in Wuyuan County of Shangrao City has actively promoted the development of the rice wine industry in recent years, creating job opportunities for local villagers. The village produces about 250,000 kilograms of rice wine annually, with an output value exceeding six million yuan (about 0.9 million U.S. dollars). In 2020, the Kengtou rice wine brewing technique was included in the fifth batch of the municipal intangible cultural heritage list for representative items of Shangrao City. item.title: Tokens hit e-commerce shelves, highlighting shifts in China's consumption pattern
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
Tokens hit e-commerce shelves, highlighting shifts in China's consumption pattern Staff members inspect cabinet racks at a data center in Xiangyang, central China's Hubei province. (Photo/Wang Hu) This year's "Double 11" shopping festival in China welcomed a new addition to consumers' shopping carts. Alongside traditional goods such as daily necessities, digital products, and home appliances, intangible tokens have made their way onto e-commerce platforms, emerging as a popular new item. Tokens are the basic units for measuring large language model inference. Data from e-commerce platform JD.com shows that during a two-hour livestream hosted by JD.com's 3C digital sales team on Nov. 2, sales of token packages surged 20-fold month-on-month. Data from Alibaba's online marketplace Tmall shows that on the same day, a livestreaming room on the platform set a sales record of 2 trillion tokens in half an hour. The appearance of tokens on e-commerce platforms vividly reflects how artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly integrating into production and daily life. It also offers a glimpse into China's innovation-driven pursuit of high-quality development. Looked at from a closer perspective, it serves as a powerful testament to consumption structure upgrading. A staff member trains a robot to collect garbage at the Guizhou Artificial Intelligence Data Factory in Guiyang, southwest China's Guizhou province. (Photo/Yuan Fuhong) An expanding number of consumption scenarios are deeply integrating with AI, including human-computer interaction powered by wearable smart devices, and AI agents assisting with daily office work. Paying for tokens is, in essence, paying for greater efficiency, creative empowerment, and intelligent services. It reflects a shift in consumer demand from traditional physical goods to digital services and intelligent experiences. Data from China's National Bureau of Statistics shows that in the first three quarters of this year, total retail sales of consumer goods and services rose 2.6 percent year-on-year, with retail sales of services growing by 5 percent. Highlights of structural shifts in consumption were particularly striking. Big data released by the country's Ministry of Commerce shows that in the first three quarters, sales revenue of smart glasses on major platforms surged 1.1 times, exoskeleton assistive devices increased 46.4 percent, and embodied AI robots grew by 22.6 percent. As consumers willingly invest in intelligent lifestyles and production methods, their willingness to spend on tokens follows naturally. As consumption extends from traditional physical goods to smart devices and services, it not only meets upgraded consumer demands, but also expands the breadth and depth of domestic demand. Citizens shop for smart glasses at a store in Tongren city, southwest China's Guizhou province. (Photo/Shen Yikai) Looked at from a practical perspective, paying for tokens is a vivid practice of accelerating the creation of new quality productive forces. The entities that stockpile tokens are not only individuals, but also micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises. Spanning software development and product design to marketing and promotion, the application scenarios of AI among small and medium-sized enterprises are continuously expanding. Behind this trend lies the real economy's pressing demand for intelligent transformation. Against the backdrop of the deep integration of scientific and industrial innovation, AI is emerging as a critical force reshaping future development patterns. In trade and logistics, smart product selection and multi-language real-time translation are boosting the quality and efficiency of cross-border trade. On production floors, industrial quality inspection and supply chain scheduling have become more precise and efficient thanks to AI. AI is no longer merely an option but an increasingly essential tool, accelerating digital transformation across industries. As large models move from laboratories to production floors, computing power has become an indispensable factor of production, much like electricity during the industrial age, injecting strong momentum into the transformation from old growth drivers into new ones. Looked at from a deeper perspective, paying for tokens is a concentrated manifestation of the advantages of China's super-large market. As large AI models continuously iterate through R&D and find widespread application in production and consumption, China's massive market serves as both an expansive testing ground for emerging products and business formats, and a fertile breeding ground for the rise of new forms of the intelligent economy. The strong sales of tokens during the "Double 11" shopping festival vividly show that a massive user base is proactively embracing intelligent production and lifestyles. Data offers compelling proof. China's average daily token calls skyrocketed from 100 billion at the beginning of 2024 to over 140 trillion in March this year. In a super-large market, massive application scenarios can support large models in achieving rapid iteration at lower costs, fully unlocking the scale advantages of the intelligent economy. The interplay between market advantages and innovation vitality is making computing power increasingly accessible to ordinary users, rather than just businesses, while strengthening China's competitive edge in the AI era. Putting tokens on e-commerce shelves is merely a starting point. Improving safety governance and strengthening after-sales service to ensure that intelligent consumption truly benefits everyone remains a task that requires the joint efforts of all sides. As AI technology continues to advance and application scenarios keep expanding, converging growth drivers will continuously fuel China's high-quality economic development. item.title: China launches Shenzhou-24 spaceship to Tiangong space station with first foreign astronaut on board
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
China launches Shenzhou-24 spaceship to Tiangong space station with first foreign astronaut on board The Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship, atop a Long March-2F carrier rocket, blasts off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, Nov. 25, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Minggang) JIUQUAN, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- China launched the Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship on Wednesday, sending three astronauts, including a Pakistani payload specialist, to its orbiting Tiangong space station. The spaceship, atop a Long March-2F carrier rocket, blasted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China. The astronauts aboard the spaceship are mission commander and spacecraft pilot Tang Hongbo, flight engineer Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first-ever foreign astronaut to visit Tiangong. The Shenzhou-24 mission marks the first joint flight consisting of Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program. item.title: Xi urges advancing building of Party regulations, institutions
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
Xi urges advancing building of Party regulations, institutions BEIJING, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged continuous and high-quality advancement in the building of regulations and institutions of the Communist Party of China (CPC), and upholding rule-based governance as the basic approach to governing the Party. Xi, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a recent instruction on the work related to Party regulations and institutions. Xi said the CPC has made solid efforts and achieved notable achievements in strengthening Party regulations and institutions over the past five years. To provide institutional guarantees for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance and ensuring the Party remains the strong leadership core in building socialism with Chinese characteristics, Xi urged enhanced efforts in the systematic integration, education and enforcement of Party institutions, as well as in improving the alignment and coordination of Party rules and regulations with state laws and regulations. Xi's instruction was conveyed at a national meeting on the work related to Party regulations held in Beijing on Tuesday and Wednesday. Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and a member of the Secretariat of the CPC Central Committee, attended and addressed the meeting. Running the Party through institutions and regulations is one of the core meanings of Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building, Cai noted, calling for efforts to enhance the level of running the Party through regulations across the board.
